channel.title: WireMinute | Breaking News & Live World Updates
channel.description: Breaking news and live world updates from WireMinute: world, politics, business, technology, sports and health, reported in our own words and updated every minute.

item.title: Pregnant US Citizen Pepper-Sprayed and Pinned to Ground by ICE Agents in California
item.description: A pregnant American woman was pepper-sprayed and forced face down onto the pavement by immigration agents outside a county jail in California, after telling them she was pregnant, video of the encounter shows. She was held for several hours and released without charge.

item.title: Kuwait Says Its Air Defences Are Engaging Hostile Drones as Gulf Fighting Widens
item.description: Kuwait said early on Wednesday that its air defences were engaging hostile drones over the country, as the war between the United States and Iran spread to a new Gulf front and Bahrain issued a fresh public safety alert.

item.title: Ecuadorian Fishermen Take Trump Administration to Court Over Drone Strike on Their Boat
item.description: Sixteen Ecuadorian fishermen have sued the Trump administration in a United States federal court, saying a drone strike wrongly targeted their fishing boat in the Pacific in March, sank it and left two of the crew with serious burns.

item.title: Gaza Ceasefire Could Collapse Without Action, Peace Board Warns UN
item.description: The board overseeing the Gaza ceasefire has warned the United Nations Security Council that the year-old truce could collapse without immediate action, saying a ceasefire that delivers nothing visible cannot be sustained indefinitely.

item.title: Quad Leaders Warn on Economic Coercion in First Summit in Two Years
item.description: The leaders of the United States, India, Japan and Australia warned of grave concerns about economic coercion at their first full summit in two years in Manila, and announced five joint initiatives, including a first maritime surveillance exercise and an 85 million dollar push on trusted artificial intelligence.

item.title: Europe Bets on Light-Based Chips to Catch the Next Wave in Semiconductors
item.description: Europe is pouring hundreds of millions of euros into chips that compute with light instead of electricity, betting that the next generation of semiconductors will be photonic and that the continent can lead it rather than chase a silicon race it has already lost.

item.title: Haitians March in Support of Bukele's Troops as El Salvador Plans Withdrawal
item.description: Crowds have marched through several Haitian cities in support of El Salvador's troop deployment, a day after San Salvador said its forces would leave once four kidnapped Salvadoran airmen are found.

item.title: New York Shortlists Ten Developers for First New Nuclear Plant in Decades
item.description: New York has named the ten companies that will compete to build the state's first new nuclear power plant in decades, picking them from 21 bids for at least one gigawatt of new atomic capacity in the north of the state.

item.title: Pentagon Tells Allies Ukraine Deep Strikes Do Not Work as Germany and Britain Push Back
item.description: The Pentagon's policy chief has told Ukraine's allies that Kyiv's long-range strikes deep inside Russia are not working, setting off an open split with Germany and Britain at a meeting of the country's military backers in Brussels.

item.title: Kahana Takes Speaker's Chair as Eisenkot Bloc Seizes Control of Israel's Parliament
item.description: Israel's parliament has elected Matan Kahana of Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party as its new speaker, handing the opposition bloc control of the legislative agenda in the first major defeat for Benjamin Netanyahu since last month's deadlocked election.

item.title: Nvidia's New Boss Says Ambition Has Never Been Greater as Revenue More Than Doubles
item.description: Nvidia more than doubled its revenue and profit in its first results since founder Jensen Huang resigned, beating Wall Street forecasts on every measure and lifting its outlook for the rest of the year.

item.title: Tear Gas and Water Cannon as Brussels Student March Turns Tense
item.description: Thousands of students and teachers marched through Brussels on Tuesday against higher university tuition fees, education reforms and funding cuts, in a demonstration that ended with police firing tear gas and turning water cannon on the crowds.

item.title: Navy Chief Tells Senators the Iran War Is Straining the Fleet
item.description: The acting head of the US Navy has told senators the war with Iran is straining the service, as lawmakers from both parties pressed him on long deployments, dwindling weapons stocks and the cost of the naval blockade.

item.title: Carney and Xi Widen Tariff Relief as Canada and China Deepen Trade Reset
item.description: Canada and China have agreed to widen tariff relief on hundreds of millions of dollars of goods, as Prime Minister Mark Carney met President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen and both sides pushed their trade reset further.

item.title: Record Surf Pounds California Coast as El Nino Swell Floods Beaches and Closes Piers
item.description: Giant waves fuelled by a strengthening El Nino have battered California's coast for a fourth straight day, flooding streets, damaging piers and closing beaches, with forecasters warning another round of heavy surf is on the way.

item.title: WHO Closes Climate and Health Challenge After Showcasing 24 Projects From Around the World
item.description: The World Health Organization has closed its Climate and Health Co-benefits Challenge, a global call for climate projects outside the health sector that are already delivering measurable gains for people’s health.

item.title: China Sacks Gene-Editing Scientist After Six-Year-Old Dies in Trial
item.description: China has sacked the scientist who led an experimental gene-editing trial in which a six-year-old girl died, after an official investigation found his team ignored safety warnings and hid the death from the journal that published their research.

item.title: Classified NSA Network Back Up After Outage, US Official Says
item.description: The National Security Agency's classified internal communications network is back up after an outage on Tuesday that forced the agency to stagger staff arrivals at its Fort Meade headquarters, a US official said.

item.title: Russian Military Transport Plane Crashes in Siberia, Killing All 19 on Board
item.description: A Russian military transport plane crashed in southwestern Siberia on Tuesday, killing all 19 people on board, Russia's Defence Ministry said, after the aircraft caught fire and came down near a village in the Kemerovo region.

item.title: US Confirms Strike on Iran Missile Site on Qeshm Island in Strait of Hormuz
item.description: The United States has confirmed that its fighter aircraft struck an Iranian missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island on Tuesday, after Tehran first reported the attack and Washington stayed silent for hours.

item.title: Turnout Falls Sharply as French Public Workers Strike Over Pay
item.description: Turnout fell sharply across France on Tuesday as public sector workers staged a nationwide strike over pay, with official figures showing far fewer marchers than at the last day of action earlier this month.

item.title: North Macedonia and Greece Foil Alleged Iran-Linked Assassination Plot
item.description: North Macedonia and Greece say they have foiled an alleged assassination plot in Greece directed by an Iranian citizen linked to Tehran's security services, arresting five people in a joint operation announced on Tuesday.

item.title: Southern Separatists Mobilise to Defend Aden as Houthi Forces Close In
item.description: Southern separatists in Yemen have launched a mobilisation campaign to defend Aden as Houthi fighters advance to within about 60 kilometres of the city, the seat of the country's internationally recognised government.

item.title: US Loses Measles Elimination Status After 26 Years as Cases Hit Three-Decade High
item.description: The United States has lost its measles elimination status after 26 years, after health officials found the virus had spread continuously in the country for more than a year, with cases this year at their highest in more than three decades.

item.title: Student Movement Takes Its Seats in Serbia's Parliament After Historic Election Win
item.description: Serbia's student-led movement took its seats in parliament on Tuesday, turning nearly two years of street protest into the country's governing majority and ending 14 years of rule by Aleksandar Vucic's party.

item.title: Bessent Wins the China Chip Fight as Treasury Writes New Curbs Over Lutnick
item.description: A rift between Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over sales of advanced computer chips to China spilled into public view on Monday, as the administration issued tough new curbs written by Bessent's department rather than the Commerce Department that normally oversees export controls.

item.title: Malicious Code Smuggled Into Website Testing Tool Reached 178 Organisations
item.description: Attackers turned a widely used website testing service into a channel for malicious code on Monday, reaching the websites of 178 organisations, including some of the most visited sites on the internet, security researchers have found.

item.title: Trump Says Kim Would Like to Join China Summit, Opening Door to First Meeting in Seven Years
item.description: President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that North Korean leader Kim Jong Un would like to attend this week's Asia-Pacific summit in China, leaving open the possibility of the first meeting between the two men in seven years.

item.title: Britain Sanctions Eight Israeli Settlement Firms and Gaza Aid Blocking Group
item.description: Britain has imposed sanctions on eight Israeli construction and property companies involved in building settlements in the occupied West Bank, along with the activist group Tzav 9, which blocks humanitarian aid from reaching Gaza.

item.title: 46 Hurt as Two Trains Collide Near Prague's Main Station
item.description: Two passenger trains collided on a railway bridge near Prague's main station during the morning rush hour on Tuesday, injuring 46 people, four of them critically, and halting rail services across the Czech capital.
